Senses.Explanation: Literally, the occasion or pivot and its operation. The compound occurs 564 times in 189 allowlisted texts and names the responsive action displayed or exercised in encounters. Records say that Dahui exhausted or displayed all his responsive operation before Wuzu, that another master and his interlocutor's responsive operation 'matched closely,' and that a portrait praise had Linji's responsive operation without indiscriminately carrying out staff-blows and shouts. Appraisals call it cutting, like thunder and lightning, or say it runs like thunder; instructional prose pairs living responsive operation with changing circumstances and contrasts it with dead rules. The compound also expands as 'great responsive operation' and joins recurrent predicates such as display, exhaust, match, be lively, run crosswise and lengthwise, or be fully raised. These are corpus descriptions of observable encounter conduct; the pivot or occasion graph (機) does not by itself name a student's graded capacity, and the records assign no single hidden purpose to the actions.
Senses.Note: The graph pair behaves as one nominal compound across biographies, portrait praises, appraisals, and prose. Predicative differences do not create separate referents. Related 'great pivot and great operation' (大機大用) is an intensified family form, not a second referent within this headword.

Senses.Explanation: A compound of "occasion, trigger, or responsive capacity" (機) and "circumstance or connection" (緣). In Chan records it commonly names a teacher-student encounter and, by extension, its recorded words. It appears as a section heading introducing successive exchanges, in the stable compound "question-and-answer encounters" (問答機緣), and in catalogues alongside entering-the-room encounters (入室機緣). One compilation calls the 1,700 old cases "1,700 encounters" (一千七百則機緣); the same author asks about "buddhas' and patriarchs' encounters, commonly called public cases" (佛祖機緣世稱公案者). The institutional deviation is therefore visible in record structure: an ordinary occasion or connection becomes a countable, titled public exchange preserved and revisited by the lineage.
Senses.Note: This technical sense does not turn every raw match into a formal interview. It preserves the texts' cautions: Zhongfeng lists seeking in encounters beside seeking in language and the 1,700 entangling vines, and Fangrong raises the whisk while setting "encounter question-and-answer" aside. Family check: "question-and-answer" (問答) is the reciprocal verbal exchange; "a monk asked" (僧問) is one speaker-turn formula; "enter the room" (入室) identifies the room setting; "encounter" (機緣) is the wider encounter and its record. Fitting occasion or concord is separated below as a different referent. The headword has 1,568 occurrences in 303 allowlisted texts.

Senses.Explanation: Outside the countable encounter-record use, "encounter" (機緣) names circumstances coming together or an accord between people. Zhongfeng says "the occasion is touched by chance" (機緣偶觸). A record preface praises a teacher's transmission and says his "capacities and circumstances accorded" (機緣吻合) before quoting a succession charge. These denote a convergence or fit, not a titled question-and-answer record.
Senses.Note: This sense is split under #0f.8 because a circumstance or accord is a different thing from a countable public encounter and its transcript. The two English targets are not competing interpretations of one usage; they follow two independently anchored constructions within the broader non-record sense.

AlternateTargets: the cutting edge of a response
Senses.Explanation: A two-image compound: (機) is the trigger/spring of a crossbow — the pivoting mechanism that releases at a touch — and (鋒) is the point or cutting edge of a blade. The compound is applied to people and exchanges in the record. Its observed deployments include: (a) as a measure of a person's capacity — a master's (機鋒) is called (峭峻) / (高峻) ('steep and sharp'), (迅捷) / (敏捷) / (捷疾) ('quick and nimble'), (不可觸) ('cannot be touched'); and (b) as the actual thrust traded in dialogue — (互換機鋒), teacher and student 'trading pivotal points.' The similes are all speed-and-edge, with Zen-scoped grep counts: (睦州機鋒)。(如閃電相似) ('like a flash of lightning'; once, T48n2003), (霹靂機鋒) ('thunderbolt point'; once, T48n2006), (機鋒電掣) ('the point flashes like lightning'; 7 texts), and the descriptor collocations (機鋒峭峻)·(高峻) (7 hits/4 texts), (機鋒迅捷)·(迅利)·(敏捷) (75/49), (互換機鋒) (18/15), (機鋒不可觸) (19/15); (機鋒) totals 673 hits in 195 allowlist texts. The texts use (機鋒) as this descriptor of speed and edge — the released trigger and the blade's tip — and assign it no gloss beyond those two images. Deployment: (機鋒不可觸) serves as a reputation formula — (內翰蘇軾居士聞玉泉皓禪師機鋒不可觸)，(公擬抑之)，(即微服求見) (the scholar Su Shi, hearing that Yuquan Hao's 機鋒 could not be touched, planned to suppress him and visited incognito; J29nB239, also T51n2077) — and as a narrative verdict: (師於言下大悟)。(機鋒不可觸) (T51n2077). A record can sum up a master with it: (僧擬開口)，(師便打)。(其機鋒峭峻多此類) (a monk was about to open his mouth; the master struck — his 機鋒 was steep-and-sharp, and much was of this kind; X71n1419). The corpus also records the word itself asked about and left unglossed: a prince asks (相公能答機鋒者麼), the official (瞪目無言) and afterward asks the master (如何教作機鋒), who answers only (待汝悟後必知) (after you awaken you will surely know; J39nB471). Dahui records a corrective deployment of the same favorable-sounding vocabulary: after describing performance 'like a flash of lightning' where deliberation cannot arrive, the record says, 'this is called a swift pivotal edge that does not fall into the thinking root,' then immediately, 'little does one know that it is precisely identity-consciousness playing tricks with ghostly eyes' (謂之機鋒俊快不落意根。殊不知。正是業識弄鬼眼睛). Thus the corpus applies the label in praise-like reputation formulae and also explicitly criticizes what is called a swift pivotal edge; this entry does not decide what it accomplishes.
Senses.Note: Broadly attested as a descriptor across the songgu and denglu collections (碧巖錄, 人天眼目, 從容錄, 五燈會元 and the Jiaxing yulu). It is a shared critical vocabulary, not any one master's coinage, so a single corpus-wide sense is honest; no master bends the base meaning. Note the recurring pairing with (照用) (照用雷奔／機鋒電掣) and with (賓主) (賓中問主，互換機鋒); the word 'pivotal edge' (機鋒) occurs inside the recorded guest-and-host exchange.
